summary: Full E2E testing of CalyzaTech website. Backend: 7/7 pytest tests pass (root, contact valid/invalid, chat streaming for FinTech content, multi-turn memory, honest no-fabrication answer, missing session validation). Frontend: home scroll roundtrip smooth with no runtime errors; only benign WebGL/THREE deprecation warnings. Theme toggle flips body bg on all 5 pages (/, /services, /ai-factory, /case-studies, /contact) — /ai-factory and /contact keep their dark plum surfaces in both themes by design. Chat streams real GPT-5.4 replies, produces action chips, chip click navigates to /ai-factory?industry=fintech, multi-turn memory retained. Contact form shows all 5 per-field errors on empty submit and displays contact-success block on valid submission. AI Factory selector chips (healthcare/fintech/education/hospitality) all clickable; deploy steps read Discover/Design/Deploy/Scale as required. Case Studies show 4 industries with 'CASE STUDY DETAILS COMING SOON' pills and — placeholders (intentional).

issues: Console warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative/fixed/absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly' — Framer Motion useScroll target likely lacks a positioned ancestor. Not user-visible but should be fixed.
THREE.Clock deprecation warning (THREE r168+): switch to THREE.Timer at some point — cosmetic.

action_items: Optional: fix Framer Motion 'non-static position' warning by adding position:relative to the scroll container.
Optional: replace THREE.Clock with THREE.Timer to silence deprecation warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: chat_sessions is an in-memory dict — will be lost on backend restart and won't scale across workers. Fine for single-instance MVP but worth noting.
server.py: ContactMessageCreate.email is a plain str with min_length=3; no format validation. Consider EmailStr from pydantic for a real email check (currently 'a@b' would pass).
server.py: CORS allow_origins uses '*' with allow_credentials=True — browsers ignore credentials with wildcard; not a functional bug but misleading config.
server.py: LlmChat model configured as ('openai', 'gpt-5.4') — verify this model id is valid for the Emergent universal key; tests confirm it responds, so OK.
seed_data_creation: None; contact form insert leaves TEST_ record with name 'TEST User' in db.contact_messages — safe to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Contact form testids use suffixes -input/-select/-button (contact-name-input, contact-email-input, contact-industry-select, contact-message-input, contact-timeline-select, contact-submit-button). Error testids match the spec: contact-error-{name|email|industry|message|timeline}. Chat testids: chat-toggle, chat-input, chat-send, chat-panel, chat-action-{slug}. AI Factory: selector-{healthcare|fintech|education|hospitality}, deploy-step-0{1..4}. Case studies: case-status-{industry}. Backend chat endpoint requires POST /api/chat with {session_id, message}; response is SSE with 'data: {"delta":...}' and terminates with 'data: [DONE]'.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs surfaced. Scroll lag fix appears to be effective: no jank, no memory-leak console errors, only benign WebGL performance messages (GPU stall on ReadPixels during screenshot capture, expected).
